title: A token check that only runs when one authentication type is configured: every other configuration has none
index_line: T-0051 · EXEC · `if (authType == UserName) verify(token)` on a machine-to-machine SOAP endpoint, then task-driven file write · c# · corroborated
invariant_violated: A conditional guard is assumed to be a guard. `if (authType == UserName) { VerifyToken(token); }` reads as 'authenticate machine callers when they use the username scheme' and is written as an *improvement* — but it makes verification a property of configuration. In every deployment where the other scheme is in use, the endpoint that was meant to be authenticated is simply open.

mechanism.does: the attacker posts a SOAP request to the staging/synchronisation endpoint that replicas use to exchange content
the request body is deserialised into a synchronisation task and handed to the task runner
the token check is wrapped in a configuration comparison, so it executes only for one of the supported authentication types
for any other configuration the verification branch never runs and the request proceeds unauthenticated, straight into the task runner
the task's parameters drive a file write into a media/staging location under the application root
the written handler is requested and executes in the application's context

source.http.body.value: the SOAP envelope — the interesting part is the task payload inside it, not the action header

guard.none.value: the token check exists in the source and is skipped by configuration; the guard is conditional, which is the same as absent

sink.file.write.value: the task runner's media/staging write, which accepts a path and a type from the task data

encoding.string.value: SOAP namespaces and the task XML shape; the request has to look like a legitimate replica to reach the runner

preconditions.expr: a machine-to-machine sync/staging endpoint is present and enabled
its verification is conditional on a configured authentication type
the endpoint answers without a session in the deployed configuration

success: an unauthenticated SOAP POST reaches the task runner — the response is a task-level error, not an auth error
a file appears under the staging/media directory with content from the task payload
requesting the written file returns executed output rather than source
failure_like: the endpoint is disabled, or verification runs before the branch rather than inside it
the task runner validates the path and type against an allow-list
false_positive: an auth error from the endpoint — that is the guard running; the bug needs the other configuration
a 200 with an empty SOAP fault: the endpoint answered, but check whether the runner was reached

hazards: grep for guards inside conditionals: `if (config == X) verify()` is a missing guard in every other config, and it looks like diligence in review
machine-to-machine endpoints age badly — they were written for a trusted peer and the trust assumption outlived the network it was written for
the write half is usually an upload or media handler that trusts the task data; the two defects compose into pre-auth RCE
distinct from T-0046 (endpoint never had a check) and T-0045 (the check is applied to the wrong object): here the check exists but is conditional
non_transfers: endpoints that verify before branching on configuration
deployments where the sync service is off (the vendor's default) — establish that the endpoint is live before claiming reachability
